public_rationale: The announced schedule supports Zitron's expectation, and an October article says the full rate applied from July. However, that article identifies no new verification beyond the earlier filing. The retrieved primary records do not isolate July charges. The deadline has elapsed, but the evidence does not establish either implementation or failure.
limitations: The review tests the charge taking effect, not the precise cash-transfer date.
Later expanded commitments cannot establish the amount charged in July.
No inference of nonpayment is drawn from missing public records.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Starting in July 2026, Anthropic will pay SpaceX $1.25 billion a month ($15 billion a year) for compute, on top of its other compute deals.
conditions: on top of Google, Amazon and Microsoft deals

statement.excerpt: In July, Anthropic will start paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month, - or $15 billion a year, - on top of all of its other compute deals with Google, Amazon and Microsoft.

from_speaker: will start paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month
on top of all of its other compute deals with Google, Amazon and Microsoft
our_interpretation: July means July 2026, with the latest possible start date July 31.
The plain reading is that the full monthly charge began applying in July. It does not require disclosure of the bank-transfer day.
The annual figure restates the monthly rate over twelve months; it does not assert that $15 billion was paid during calendar 2026.
The other compute deals are an additive part of the claim, not an antecedent that makes this a conditional forecast.
A pre-July contract schedule alone establishes the plan, not that the full charge subsequently began.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records confirm that the $1.25 billion monthly SpaceX charge began applying during July 2026 while Anthropic retained the other named compute arrangements.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records show that the July full-rate charge did not begin, began at a different amount, or replaced rather than supplemented the named arrangements.
